verdict.rationale: Kimi is itself an AI assistant and coding agent (Kimi Code CLI, Desktop, and IDE agent), so it fills the MCP-client role, and serving tools to other agents as an MCP server is a different product role. Nothing in the evidence shows Kimi running as an MCP server, such as an 'mcp serve' mode or a hosted MCP endpoint. The ACP protocol lets editors drive the CLI, but that is not an MCP server.
